nodes.summary: A cost record for the Floyd–Warshall algorithm is a pair of natural numbers: the number of initialization events (input matrix cells copied into the initial distance table) and the number of min-plus transition events (table entries updated).
nodes.title: Floyd–Warshall cost record

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $D$ be the distance matrix computed by Floyd–Warshall from $w$. For all vertices $s$ and $t$, $D(s, t) = \infty$ if and only if there is no weighted path from $s$ to $t$, that is, no nonempty vertex sequence from $s$ to $t$ in which every consecutive pair has finite weight.
nodes.title: Floyd–Warshall reports $\infty$ exactly for unreachable pairs

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, suppose that $w$ has no negative cycle, and let $D$ be the distance matrix computed by Floyd–Warshall from $w$. Then for all vertices $s$ and $t$ and every weighted path $p$ from $s$ to $t$ (a nonempty vertex sequence from $s$ to $t$ in which every consecutive pair has finite weight), $D(s, t)$ is at…
nodes.title: No path is shorter than the Floyd–Warshall distance

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $D$ be the distance matrix computed by Floyd–Warshall from $w$. If $D(s, t) = d$ for vertices $s$, $t$ and an integer $d$, then there is a weighted path from $s$ to $t$ (a nonempty vertex sequence from $s$ to $t$ in which every consecutive pair has finite weight) whose weight, the sum of the…
nodes.title: Finite Floyd–Warshall distances are attained

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, suppose that $w$ has no negative cycle, and let $D$ be the distance matrix computed by Floyd–Warshall from $w$. Then for all vertices $s$ and $t$, $D(s, t)$ is at most the weight of every weighted path from $s$ to $t$, and either $D(s, t) = \infty$ or $D(s, t)$ is the weight of some weighted path from…
nodes.title: Floyd–Warshall computes shortest-path distances

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $D$ be the distance matrix computed by Floyd–Warshall from $w$. If $w$ has no negative cycle, then the negative-diagonal check on $D$ returns false, that is, $D(v, v) \ge 0$ for every vertex $v$.
nodes.title: Without negative cycles, Floyd–Warshall finds no negative diagonal entry

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $D$ be the distance matrix computed by Floyd–Warshall from $w$. If $D(v, v) < 0$ for some vertex $v$, then $w$ has a negative cycle: a vertex sequence $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_m$ with $m \ge 1$ and $v_m = v_0$, whose vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{m-1}$ are pairwise distinct, in which every consecutive pair…
nodes.title: A negative diagonal entry in Floyd–Warshall reveals a negative cycle

nodes.summary: For every $n$ and every $n \times n$ matrix of weights in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{+\infty\}$, the Floyd–Warshall algorithm performs exactly $n^2$ initialization events, one for each ordered pair of vertices.
nodes.title: Initialization count of Floyd–Warshall

nodes.summary: For every $n$ and every $n \times n$ matrix of weights in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{+\infty\}$, the total number of events counted by the Floyd–Warshall algorithm, initialization events plus min-plus transition events, is exactly $n^2 + n^3$.
nodes.title: Floyd–Warshall performs $n^2 + n^3$ steps

nodes.summary: For every $n$ and every $n \times n$ matrix of weights in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{+\infty\}$, the Floyd–Warshall algorithm performs exactly $n^3$ min-plus transition events, one for each triple $(k, i, j)$ of vertices.
nodes.title: Transition count of Floyd–Warshall

nodes.summary: Given an $n \times n$ matrix $w$ of weights in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{+\infty\}$ indexed by the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$, the Floyd–Warshall algorithm starts from the table with $d^{(0)}_{ii} = \min(w_{ii}, 0)$ and $d^{(0)}_{ij} = w_{ij}$ for $i \ne j$, and for $k = 0, \dots, n - 1$ computes the table $d^{(k+1)}_{ij} = \min\bigl(d^{(k)}_{ij}, d^{(k)}_{ik} + d^{(k)}_{kj}\bigr)$. It returns the matrix $d^{(n)}$…
nodes.title: Floyd–Warshall algorithm

nodes.summary: An $n \times n$ matrix $w$ of weights in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{+\infty\}$ has a negative cycle when some list of vertices is a negative cycle for $w$.
nodes.title: Matrices with a negative cycle

nodes.summary: For every $n \times n$ matrix $d$ with entries in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{+\infty\}$, the negative-diagonal test on $d$ returns true if and only if $d_{vv} < 0$ for some vertex $v$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the negative-diagonal test

nodes.summary: For an $n \times n$ matrix $d$ with entries in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{+\infty\}$, the negative-diagonal test on $d$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when $d_{vv} < 0$ for some vertex $v$.
nodes.title: Negative-diagonal test

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a list of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ has all its intermediate vertices below $k$ when every entry of the list other than its first and its last is less than $k$.
nodes.title: Intermediate vertices below a bound

nodes.summary: For an $n \times n$ matrix $w$ of weights in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{+\infty\}$, a list of vertices $v_0, \dots, v_m$ is a negative cycle when $m \ge 1$, $v_m = v_0$, every weight $w_{v_i v_{i+1}}$ with $i < m$ is finite, the vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{m-1}$ are pairwise distinct, and the path weight $\sum_{i < m} w_{v_i v_{i+1}}$ is negative.
nodes.title: Negative cycles

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$, let $k$ be a natural number, let $s$ and $t$ be vertices and let $d \in \mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$. A weighted path from $s$ to $t$ is a nonempty list of vertices that starts at $s$, ends at $t$ and has $w(u, v) \ne \infty$ for every pair of consecutive vertices $u, v$; its weight is the sum of these…
nodes.title: Stage-$k$ shortest-path weight

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$, and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. A list of vertices $p$ is a weighted path from $s$ to $t$ when $p$ is nonempty, its first entry is $s$, its last entry is $t$, and $w(u, v) \ne \infty$ for every pair of consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$.
nodes.title: Finite-weight vertex path in a weight matrix

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$. Then $w$ has no negative cycle when there is no list of vertices $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_m$ with $m \ge 1$ such that $v_m = v_0$, the vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{m-1}$ are pairwise distinct, $w(v_{i-1}, v_i) \ne \infty$ for $1 \le i \le m$, and $w(v_0, v_1) + \cdots + w(v_{m-1}, v_m) < 0$.
nodes.title: Weight matrices without negative cycles

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign to each ordered pair of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ a weight in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$. The weight of a list of vertices $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_m$ with $m \ge 1$ is $w(v_0, v_1) + w(v_1, v_2) + \cdots + w(v_{m-1}, v_m)$, computed in $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ where adding $\infty$ gives $\infty$. The empty list and every single-vertex list have weight $0$.
nodes.title: Weight of a vertex path in an extended-integer weight matrix

nodes.summary: The total of a Floyd–Warshall cost record is its number of initialization events plus its number of min-plus transition events.
nodes.title: Total Floyd–Warshall cost

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
